newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: Aegon to pursue acquistions selectively.
newsitem.headline: Aegon to pursue acquistions selectively.

text.p: Dutch insurer Aegon NV said on Friday it would continue to pursue a highly selective acquisitions policy, targetting healthy companies in countries where it already had a significant presence.
"Acquisitions are the icing on the cake...We will look first to countries where we already have a strong foothold," chairman Kees Storm told a news conference on the company's 1996 results.
Storm said Aegon's first priority was to generate organic growth, followed by acquisitions in countries where it already operated and thirdly "greenfield" operations.

Aegon derives the lion's share of its revenues from the Netherlands, the United States and Britain where its majority-owned Scottish Equitable unit is the biggest private pensions provider though independent financial advisers.

But Storm said Aegon would not be focusing primarily on Britain when it came to new takeovers. "We would be highly selective if we were to acquire something in Britain at all, because Scottish Equitable is performing so well," he said.
"We would only look at proud, healthy companies...But if an attractive opportunity were to come along, we would not close our eyes to it," he said.
